subject: Urgent: AtlasHealth live stream disconnects causing retry surge
messages:
From: Samira Khanna <samira.khanna@atlashealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: support@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production incidents — sudden increase in 5xx/429 + streaming disconnects

Jonas,

We’re seeing a surge of 5xx and 429 responses across several production routes since ~07:30 PT and live chat streams are being dropped mid-conversation. Client teams report a retry loop on our side that doubled request volume and worsened latency. We attached a sample HAR and server logs. This is impacting triage workflows and patient-facing chat sessions.

Key impact: intermittent idle disconnects after ~28-32s, client-side timeouts at ~30s, and repeated reconnect attempts from our SDK (exponential with jitter) — leading to a retry storm.

We need an incident-level response and exec visibility. Our CISO (david.jones@atlashealth.com) is looped in. Please advise next steps and whether you will open an incident bridge.

—Samira
Customer Success Manager, AtlasHealth

Attachment: atlas_stream_logs_0528.zip (contains server logs and truncated stack traces)
Attachment: client-trace-20260528.har (client network traces)
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khanna <samira.khanna@atlashealth.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incidents — sudden increase in 5xx/429 + streaming disconnects

Samira — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments. I’m escalating to our SRE and CS leads now.

Immediate next steps:
- I’ve opened ticket JIRA INF-7689 and uploaded your logs.
- Marcus will coordinate a live debug session; can you confirm a 30–60 minute window for sharing screens?
- Rishi — can you initial-check ingress throttles, autoscale decisions, and any recent routing changes in the last 2 hours?

Samira: we’ll put an incident bridge in place if we see continuing 5xx/429 trends or if streams remain unstable. I’ll keep you posted on ETA for a bridge.

Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incidents — sudden increase in 5xx/429 + streaming disconnects

Quick findings from a first pass:
- Metrics: Starting ~07:25 PT we saw a sharp uptick in 429s on the chat-stream router (route: /v1/chat/stream). Error rate spiked from baseline ~0.4% to ~6.8%.
- Autoscale: No failed scale events, but queue depth climbed — latency p90 increased from 120ms to 980ms prior to retries.
- Throttling: We have a burst throttle threshold that appears to have been hit by connection churn + repeated reconnects; this explains the 429s.
- Streaming idle disconnect: Server keepalive checker logged EOFs at ~28-33s for affected streams; looks like a connection tear before max-idle.

Hypothesis: a client-side timeout of 30s is racing with our keepalive/idle-window resulting in clients reconnecting and amplifying load. The reconnects plus backpressure produce transient 429s and some server-side 5xx where overloaded worker threads aborted.

Immediate mitigations I’m proposing:
1) Temporarily relax burst-throttle for the AtlasHealth account for the next 2 hours.
2) Enable a short-lived sticky-routing variant (pin to a healthy worker pool) to reduce rehydration overhead on reconnects.
3) Ask Atlas to increase client timeout to 45s as a short-term workaround to avoid racing the idle disconnect.

I’ll stand by on the bridge. Marcus — can you draft the ACL change for relaxation and coordinate with infra?

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: monica.patel@redwood.ai
To: Samira Khanna <samira.khanna@atlashealth.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incidents — sudden increase in 5xx/429 + streaming disconnects

Samira — I’m available to join the debug session at 09:30 PT. We can also share an annotated runbook during the call. A couple of asks from our side:
- If you can provide the SDK version and the exact client timeout setting (we saw 30s in the traces), that helps.
- Please confirm whether retries are using exponential backoff and the max retry cap.

We’ll try Rishi’s mitigations immediately after the call (relax throttles + sticky routing). If Atlas approves, Jonas — can you confirm Atlas will temporarily permit a client timeout change?

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incidents — temporary throttle relaxation applied

On the bridge: applied temporary ACL relaxation for account DL-2024-ATH-09 (burst limit raised by 2x). Pinned streaming routes to warm worker pool (sticky routing) for 30 minutes. Monitoring metrics now.

Early observations (10:00 PT): 429 rate down to ~1.5%, p90 latency improving to ~340ms. We still see occasional EOFs at ~29–31s. I’ve uploaded server-side snippets to the shared drive link.

Attachment: atlas_stream_logs_0528.zip (updated)

—Marcus
SRE Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khanna <samira.khanna@atlashealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: david.jones@atlashealth.com, monica.patel@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production incidents — follow-up and exec summary

Jonas / team — thanks for rapid response and the bridge yesterday. AtlasHealth saw meaningful improvement after the throttle relaxation and sticky routing; 429s fell and customer-facing chat timeouts dropped by ~85%. The engineering team accepted the interim client timeout bump to 45s while Redwood implements a server-side idle-window adjustment and better keepalive handling.

David (CISO) asked for a short executive summary of root cause and remediation steps for our security/Risk team. Could you provide a one-page summary and any post-incident artifacts (JIRA ticket, logs, timeline)?

Samira
Customer Success Manager, AtlasHealth

P.S. Related items to include in the exec summary: reason for retry amplification, explanation of why idle disconnects happen near 30s, and plan for permanent fix (server keepalive tuning + SDK guidance).
